sections.hypothesis: Weeks that start after a coin's news tone improved (the average GDELT tone of the last 7 known days above the 28 days before) are followed by better BTC and ETH returns than weeks after it didn't, by more than costs, and not only because tone follows price.
sections.rationale: Who pays: readers who act on the news slowly, mostly retail, buying over the days after coverage turns better, from whoever sells to them before that coverage is priced in. Outside evidence: Tetlock (Giving Content to Investor Sentiment, Journal of Finance 2007): pessimism in the Wall Street Journal's daily market column predicted downward pressure on the Dow the next day, then a reversal within the week. Garcia (Sentiment during Recessions, Journal of Finance 2013): news sentiment predicted stock returns, mostly in recessions. In crypto the evidence is weak, and the note says so: a search on 2026-11-24 found no peer-reviewed study of GDELT tone and crypto returns. There are only unpublished theses: one (Helsinki) finds news tone moves Bitcoin at a weekly frequency, and one (Vaasa, 2025) finds a same-day effect that fades by 7 days. Weak points, stated now: (1) Tetlock's effect reverses within a week, so at a weekly horizon it may cancel out. (2) Tone follows price (in Tetlock, low returns came before pessimism), so 'improving tone' may only be last week's rise, and weekly momentum failed out of sample here; the control below tests exactly that. (3) GDELT's set of sources grew over 2017-25, and the queries 'bitcoin' and 'ethereum' match any article that uses the word. Independence from the pursued strategies (expected, written before the run): high. If tone mostly follows price, the on-weeks will mostly follow rising weeks, and the signal will be the trend bet again. I expect at least 60% of on-weeks to follow a rising week, against about 50% of off-weeks. The control decides; the overlap is reported. Family: a signal from outside the price, not a rejected family (not a pullback, chart pattern or reversal). Disclosed: the same family has failed four times here (Wikipedia attention, Coinbase premium, the options variance premium, dollar liquidity). Luke chose news tone (2026-11-14). Nothing about tone against returns has been looked at: while the data downloaded, only its dates and row counts were printed.
sections.rules: kestrel signal-study news-tone BTCUSDT ETHUSDT --research <this note>. Data: daily average tone from GDELT's DOC 2.0 API (mode timelinetone; query 'bitcoin' for BTCUSDT, 'ethereum' for ETHUSDT; kestrel.data.news, data/news/). Day D's tone counts only from D+2 00:00 UTC, once the day is complete and published. At each Sunday daily close (UTC) the signal is on when the mean tone of the 7 latest known days is above the mean of the 28 days before them. If any of those 35 days is missing, the week is unknown and skipped, never filled. Outcome: the log return from that close to the next Sunday's close; weeks with a missing bar are skipped. Bars: Binance daily, from listing to before 2025-11-01, never the holdout. BTC and ETH are pooled (they move together, so the effective sample is smaller than the count). The run waits until both coins' tone reaches 2025-10-31; the command refuses before then. Run once.
sections.falsification: PROCEED only if all three hold: P(spread > 0) is at least 90% (bootstrap); the spread (mean week after 'on' minus mean week after 'off') beats one round trip of costs (about 0.22%); and the independence control holds. Otherwise KILL. The control, fixed here: the spread is also measured separately in weeks whose past week rose and in weeks whose past week fell, and PROCEED needs it positive in both. If it lives in only one half, the signal is momentum (or dip-buying, a rejected family) under another name, and that is a KILL, said plainly. One-sided: worse weeks after improving tone (Tetlock's reversal) is a KILL here, recorded as found. Trading that would mean buying after the news worsens, which needs a new note, disclosed as close to dip-buying. A PROCEED leads to a strategy note on the full scorecard; BTC and ETH's holdout years are spent, so it would be judged forward on paper. A KILL ends the idea. Also reported, deciding nothing: how many weeks GDELT's gaps cost, and the overlap with the pursued strategies.
sections.parameters: None to choose. The 7-day-against-28-day rule has been in the code since 2026-11-14, before any tone data existed; it is the attention study's shape. Also fixed: Sunday closes (UTC), the D+2 rule, 5,000 bootstrap resamples, seed 0.
sections.costs: Hurdle about 0.22%: one round trip of the taker fee and half-spread from kestrel.toml. A study, not a strategy run: one look, logged in the findings, not a trial in the luck bar (as with the earlier signal studies). Data: GDELT, free, no key; requests rate-limited from this Mac.
